comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Asked by the owner on 2026-10-17: was a 9-minute gate right for a project this size? The Rust suite was about 400 of the gate's 540 s, because `cargo test --workspace` runs one test binary at a time and the seam binary's 218 tests take turns behind one lock (one session per process).

Landed: `./dev` prints a step table at the end of every run (kept in target/gate/steps.txt), and `tools/run-tests.py` runs the test binaries side by side, each seam and daemon test in a process of its own, longest first, 1.5 jobs per core. No new tool: nextest measured the same speed at equal concurrency and does not run doc tests.

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| build | 40.4 s | 9.4 s |
| test: Rust discovery | 73.7 s | 9.2 s |
| test: Rust suite | 407.8 s | 105.1 s |
| test: Swift | 17.7 s | 11.7 s |
| total | 543.5 s | 139.0 s |

(Before ran on a fresh build, so only the suite row compares like with like.)

Owed, stopped by the owner's call: three green full gates in a row on the final runner; regex-automata and regex-syntax at opt-level 3 in the dev profile, measured twice each way; build and discovery on fresh builds, before and after; the default job count on CI's 3-core runner. Flakes the parallelism exposed: a fake-agent race (fixed), and at 24 jobs only, a timing budget in lifecycle::, an assert in arranging:: (MIP-7, passed to its author) and one in seam windows::.
title: The gate runs its Rust test binaries side by side
